steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat butter, brown sugar, and white sugar together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs one at a time, then stir in vanilla and almond extracts.
Combine flour, baking soda, and salt in another bowl. Gradually stir flour mixture into butter mixture until blended.
Fold macadamia nuts and white chocolate into dough until evenly distributed.
Drop rounded spoonfuls of dough 2 inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets. Gently press each dough ball down slightly to help cookies spread evenly during baking.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, about 10 minutes. Cool cookies slightly on the baking sheets, then transfer to wire racks to cool completely. Enjoy!

review.reviewBody: Sooo delicious! I followed the advice of other reviewers and used 1/2 butter and 1/2 shortening. They turned out perfectly! I also substituted the almond extract with vanilla extract since I didn't have any almond extract on hand. I baked the cookies for exactly 10 minutes and pulled them out of the oven when just some of the edges were golden brown. I will definitely make these again. Update: I made this recipe again with all butter, no shortening. The cookies spread quite a bit and weren't nearly as good as when I made them with 1/2 shortening and 1/2 butter.

So good! I read most of the reviews and was really confused as to what to expect. Half of them said the cookies came out really cakey and puffy, and the other half said they were too flat. I don't like either extremes and really wanted a cookie that was right in the middle. I got it! I followed the recipe in the basics (was going to use less flour as some of the reviews stated, but when I was adding it, they looked like they needed all 2 1/2 cups), except did 1 tsp vanilla instead of half almond, and added more macadamia nuts and white chocolate chips. Used real salted butter, and it wasn't extremely softened, which I think helped. Dropped by tablespoons instead of teaspoons because teaspoons always seem too small. Baked for 9 minutes and they came out just undercooked in the middle, which is exactly how I like them. They were perfect. Hope this helps!

I e made 3 batches of these and they have all turned out amazing. The only changes I might make would be a tad more macadamia nuts and I've been making them about 2 inches in diameter and baking them for 8 minutes. My hubby likes them soft and 8 minutes is perfect for that. The ladies in my family actually made these on our girls Christmas vacay and rave about them.

100% hands down the best. This has been my go-to cookie recipe for years! An optional tip, I like to bake it for longer but turn the heat down to 150 C. This gives it a subway cookie style crunchy bottom. For the people commenting on the following: Tasteless - Dont forget to pack down the brown sugar. Maybe you didnt add enough. Also, always taste before putting it in the oven. Be happy with your flavour before you cook it. Raw - Your dough is too dry, add more butter. Hate Almond essence - dont use it.

Made these cookies for the first time, fantastic results! I used full teaspoon of vanilla, as I did not have almond extract.. Absolutely delicious! Ladies, stop using a mixer. Hand mix batter. Make sure butter is room temp.
I went with 1/2 cup of coarsely chopped macadamia nuts and let them firm in fridge (easier to work with) for 10 minutes. Also, cooked them a few extra minutes to get them golden on bottom.

To make this Keto/ Diabetic Friendly. Substitute:-Flour for Keto Flour Blend “Nature seats The Ultimate Nut Flour 1:1.Both Sugars for Monk Fruit granulated:1 cup; powdered: 1/4 cup; Monk Fruit Maple Styrup: 1/4 cup.-“Lily’s No Sugar White Chocolate Chips”-Use 1 Teasp Vanilla & 1/4 Teasp Almond extract instead-Use 3/4 Teasp Baking Powder-Use 1 Teasp Baking Soda-Add 1 extra EggBlend sugar, eggs, syrup, extracts until frothy add room temp butter until slightly chunky.Add in dry ingredients.Scoop into cookie sheet and press

I skipped the almond extract, but added one cup of shredded sweetened coconut and one teaspoon of coconut extract. I also left the macadamia nuts and white chocolate chips whole. If you like coconut then you might want to try. I doubled the recipe and they went fast!
I love this recipe. Living at 8500 feet I added an extra 1/4 cup flour and 2 tsp water. I bake them for 14 min. The almond really enhances the macadamia flavor

Really good a lot of people like it. I used dark brown sugar instead of light. I also used a whole bag of white chocolate chips and chopped about 12-15 whole macadamia nuts. When mixing the brown sugar and the butter, I used a spoon to beat and when I added the first egg, I also mixed with the spoon. Everything else was mixed with the blender.

YUMMY! I read a ton of reviews before baking these gems. First, I used all vegan butter because of lactose intolerance, and because I don’t like cooking with shortening. I also used all vanilla and no almond extract. They are crunchy on the outside and chewy and tasty on the inside. I also kept the cookie dough in the fridge between batches to stay chilled. I think this helped with spreading. I used an medium pampered chef cookie scooper and cooked for 10 minutes on 350.
I made the cookies but I added dried cranberries soaked in cranberry juice with orange zest, toasted the macadamia nuts with the white chocolate chips...EXCELLENT!!!
Followed the recipe and it came out great!
Just tastes like baked sugar. Batter spread way too much and made flat little pancakes instead of cookies. I won't use this recipe again.
Prep time, 1 hour. 15 minutes just to chop the nuts. I couldn't taste the almond extract that I paid $3,79 for. White chocolate has no flavor and macadamia nuts are boring.
